utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, sir, of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, yesterday we left off discussing some advisement that you had been received prior to being shown some photo boards during an interview with the Office of the Prosecutor in November of 2004. Do you recall also being advised at that time not to identify more than one possible suspect on one photo board?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you also recall being advised at that time that a possible suspect might not at all be on one or both of those photo boards?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you also recall at that time being advised that you should make a positive identification only if you're certain that you recognise the person?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recall, after these advisements were given, identifying a person in one of those photo boards as being a person that you saw at the Children's Rest House on 11 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please show the witness 65 ter 177.1, which is tab 8 of the binders, and perhaps could we have the witness's binder from yesterday, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Jurisic, what's being displayed before you is a photo board. Is this one of the two photo boards that you were shown during your interview on 9 November 2004?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention to some handwritten notes below. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And are those notes in your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And there's also a signature in the lower right-hand corner with a date of 9/11/04. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you see the handwritten circle around the photo depicted at number 9? What is that hand -- what does that circle indicate?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this a question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it was poorly phrased. Can I ask you, is the circle that's drawn around number 9, is that the person that you identified at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the handwritten notes are in Macedonian. Could you please read those for translation purposes?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I believe I have seen this person in the Children's Rest House as a policeman, but I'm not sure."

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we tender this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P368, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Jurisic, going back to the 11th of August, 2001, and the policemen, did they spend the night at the Children's Rest House?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And did you see these policemen the next day, which would be Sunday, 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Did you have a telephone issued to you during this time period, that is, the weekend of 10 August to 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had my own telephone. I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I guess my question was: Did you have a phone at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have a telephone, my own telephone.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And was that a mobile telephone that you also carried with you to your duty stations or command posts?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall if you had any telephone conversations with any of these policemen that you had seen at the Children's Rest House on Sunday, 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall if you were ever given a phone number of anyone from this group of police?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall providing a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 16th of November, 2004?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Would looking at that particular statement refresh your recollection as to whether or not you were given a telephone number of anyone from this group of police?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I look into the binder?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Well, I'm simply asking you, Mr. Jurisic, if looking at prior statements that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor would help you remember as to whether or not you had any -- had received any phone numbers or given any phone numbers to these police officers.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand. Your Honours, if I can make myself more precise, at this time when I arrived I know that I exchanged my telephone number with the leader of that group of police officers, as a normal thing. On other occasions when we were there, we exchanged telephone numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Why would such an exchange have been done?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In many situations, when the army acted together with the police at any place, it happened that regular ties do not -- are not functioning; that is to say, if anything needed to be done in any sense of the word, that we were able to hear each other. The same applies to all my soldiers or superiors. They had my number, my telephone number, so that we can talk to each other in case of need, because the connections which were running at that time were not ideal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall what your telephone number was during this particular time period?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what that phone number was?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 070217088 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is shown on the screen is not correct. The number is 070217008.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please show the witness 65 ter 1006, please. It's located at tab 9 of the binders. The first page in English should actually be almost what appears to be a blank page with just a number on it, which would match the Macedonian page that's being displayed right now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, drawing your attention to the document that's displayed before you, do you see the -- on the right there, there's a number, 070279417, and then right below that it says: "Outgoing calls, 1, 2, 3." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could turn, please, to page 2 of the English and the Macedonian. Is it possible to enlarge the Macedonian version so the witness could see that more clearly? I'd really like to just focus in, actually, on the top headers. Mr. Jurisic, you also have a hard copy in case the screen is a little difficult to read. What I'm going to ask is: Along the top columns of this page, it indicates, from the left going forward, "Caller", and then it has some number, the same number that we saw on the first page, and then the next column says "Called," and then the next column says "Date," and the next is "Sec," which presumably refers to seconds. The next says "Time," "Name," "Address of the caller," "Name of the called," "Last name of the called," "ID number," "Address of the called," and "Place." Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please turn to page 8 of the English, which is also page 8 of the Macedonian. I'd actually like to focus in on line 15 on this particular page. It is around the middle part of the page in Macedonian. Mr. Jurisic, do you see there, it's the 15th line, but there's a number there, "70279417" on the left, and then there's a number, "70217008", and it's around the middle of that page. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is that your phone number that you've indicated?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And following the column descriptions that we went over earlier, then, the caller would be 702-79417, and then the called person would be your number; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not quite get that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you see how I explained the columns that were described earlier?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: This left column, then, would be the caller, and then the column that indicates your number would then be the called person, according to this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then immediately to the right, it says --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, should I -- I need to clarify something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Page 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, for e-court purposes. I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then immediately to the right, it says -- the right of your number, it says "8/11/01" for August 11, 2001. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So that would indicate the date that you received the call, and then according to the next column, it's the length of time for the call, and then the next column to the right there, it says"10.30.22" would be the time of the call. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then following over, it says, in the name, "Mario Jurisic." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: So it indicates here, according to this phone record, that you received a call from this number, 702-79417, on August 11th, 2001, and you were on duty on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you remember what this call pertained to?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall if this number, which indicates the caller number on the far left, do you recall if this is the number that belonged to one of the policemen that you say you exchanged numbers with on Saturday, 11 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Are you able to recall anything about this particular conversation that you had on that day at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please turn to page 10 of the -- well, it would be page 9 of the hard copies, page 10 in e-court of the English, and page 10 in e-court for the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Jurisic -- if we could, perhaps, expand the Macedonian version so the witness could see -- I'll draw your attention to line number 10, which is about the upper half of the document, and you see again the same thing applies, in that there's a number, "70279417" that corresponds to the caller, and then there is again your number,"70217008". Do you see that, Mr. Jurisic?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And again following in line with the columns, it indicates that you received a call on August 12th, 2001, and the time was about 43 seconds. The time of the call was 3.47.14, and then it follows over to the name, your name. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And again I guess I'd ask you the same question. Do you recall any conversations that you had on the 12th of August at this time with this particular caller?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And were you on -- this time indicates -- it says "3.47.14". We don't have an" a.m." or "p.m." Were you on duty, though, at 3.47 p.m. on August 12, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And how about 3.47 a.m. on that day, were you on duty at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: On August 11th, 2001, did you spend the night at the Children's Rest House?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And presumably, then, did you also have your cellphone with you the night of August 11th, 2001, into the morning and day of August 12th, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please mark this for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P369, MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated that you do not recall having these particular phone conversations. Well, let me ask you this generally: Do you recall the substance of your phone conversations with any police officers that you had during this time period, which would be 11 August, 12 August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall having a conversation with myself and another colleague on 3 July 2007?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Would it refresh your recollection as to the substance of these conversations with the police officers that you had during this time period if you were able to review or hear what you indicated to us at that time?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And I apologise to my learned colleagues and the Chamber. We would have to distribute the proofing notes that were taken on July 3rd via hard copy because they have not been uploaded on e-court. So we have copies to distribute, with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Jurisic, I apologise. These proofing notes were taken in the English language and then read back to you in Macedonian. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention to paragraph 51, I will read to you what is indicated to see whether or not this might assist you in refreshing your recollection. In the middle part of paragraph 51, there's a sentence that begins: "As for the reference to phone conversations regarding targets, again I state that I do not remember having these phone conversations with any of these persons referred to in this paragraph. Also, the person identified in the photo board was not a leader, as I explained earlier today. The paragraph also refers to a second person which was in contact with me, but I do not remember being in contact with a second person. Also, I wish to clarify the reference to 'these people' in the third sentence from the bottom of the paragraph. 'These people' are the police. As for the second-to-last sentence in this paragraph, I wish to state that I do not remember anyone from the police contacting me on the phone." And in order to give context to this particular clarification that you provided on the 3rd of July, this is in reference to paragraph 14 of a statement that you remember making from the 16th of November, 2004. If we could please display that particular statement as well so that we get a full context and perhaps Mr. Jurisic's recollection could be refreshed. That statement is located at ERN N000-8674 through 8677, Macedonian version the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objections, Your Honour. In this way of examination of the witness, he had already thoroughly explained everything which he remembers, and in the proofing notes he has given an explanation of the course of his conversations. I don't see the basis that he be shown a statement that he had given earlier, thank you, in order to refresh his memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What are you about, Ms. Motoike?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is -- this particular proofing note was displayed before the witness because of context. He indicated the time of proofing that he did not remember, but there's another statement he also makes, so I'm trying to refresh his memory with all the available statements we have with respect to this particular question that I'm putting to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What are you having displayed now?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: The statement that the witness provided from 16th November 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And the proofing note is referring to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is referring to that, Your Honour. I was just trying to present the full context so that the witness perhaps could have his memory refreshed based on everything he said about this particular question that I'm putting to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Jurisic, drawing your attention to, I believe it's paragraph 14 of the statement dated 16 November 2004, it is page 3 of the statement, page 4 of the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies, but I cannot find the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: My apologies to you, Mr. Jurisic. We're actually displaying these statements via e-court on the screen. I'm drawing your attention to paragraph 14. Is there perhaps a way we could enlarge paragraph 14 in the Macedonian version, at least, for the witness? Thank you. Could we please also see the English? We don't have hard copies of the English. Thank you. I'm drawing your attention, Mr. Jurisic, to the middle of that paragraph. There's a sentence that starts with: "Like ...," and it says: "Like I said above, it is possible that in the above-mentioned phone conversations, these targets were also discussed to me by the police officers. Being asked, I can't remember exactly with whom I have had spoken about these targets over the phone. Like I said, the person I have identified in the photo line was a sort of leader. The second person which was in contact with me must have been a sort of deputy to first one. I haven't been in contact with ..." And if we could turn the page in the English, please. It says: " ... With these people." And during proofing you clarified that "these people" were the police: " ... Before this event, and so I know very little about them. Being asked why I was informed directly by the police on the phone, I say this was shorter than receiving the information through Despodov. I mean this in general, for the order to support in all aspects." Given these statements, Mr. Jurisic, does any of this refresh your recollection as to the substance of the conversations that you had with the policeman on the phone that particular weekend?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that my learned colleague should first ask whether he recollects whether he had such a conversation and only then to ask about the substance of this conversation, because previously the witness had not said that he had remembered having such a conversation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I believe at the moment, having read the relevant passages in the statement, the question being asked, "Does that refresh your recollection?" Now, she will either receive a "yes" or a "no" answer, I expect, and we will take it from there.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Jurisic, when you were interviewed in 2004, were the events with respect to what had occurred fresher in your mind then than as you sit here today?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I be allowed to explain some things? In 2004, as I recall, when I was interviewed, to this day I cannot remember certain things. Why is this so? Because at this period of time when the events were transpiring of 2001, I lost eight soldiers. It is as if I lost a part of me. To this day, each thought to the events of 2001, the first picture that appears in my mind is the picture of the bodies of my soldiers, of arms and legs in the field, and the rest -- and then the rest of the pictures come to my mind from which I try to form a mosaic. In 2004, when I was interviewed by the investigators of your Tribunal, they pointed out certain issues to me. The only thing I could do was confirm that perhaps such things happened. After this period, I thought about this, and I tried to form a mosaic in my head. And what I'm saying today, this is in fact what transpired, this is of what I'm sure. Of what I'm not sure of, this is the only thing I can say. I can only confirm what I am sure transpired. This is what I had to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, drawing your attention back, though, to August 12th, 2001, did the army maintain its positions at the observation points that you've already described to us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, did the army actually enter Ljuboten village on 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please display for the witness what's already been marked for identification purposes as P306. It's at tab 15 of today's binders. The Macedonian version should actually be a handwritten note, that is, N001-4665 to N001-4666.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There is a problem with the Macedonian version, it appears, Ms. Motoike. The witness has a hard copy, does he?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With the Court's permission then, can we work off the hard copy, and perhaps I have a copy we could display on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, do you see the document that's being displayed next to you on the ELMO? Actually, it should be on the screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the handwriting in this document?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is that handwriting yours?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could go down to the bottom of, I think believe, page 2 of the Macedonian version. It's page 2, I believe. Thank you. The very bottom, there should be a signature line, I believe, at the very bottom of the lower right-hand corner. Thank you. And, Mr. Jurisic, do you recognise that signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see clearly, but it's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could draw your attention to the top of page 1, the very top there, it says: "Report," and then it says: "In relation to the military activities on 12 August 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And was this a report that was drafted by you regarding your observations on 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And was this done -- was this report drafted shortly after the events transpired?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if I could just draw your attention to the first paragraph there, it says: "At 800 hours on the 12th August 2001, one could hear shots in the area of Ljuboten village. The right wing of defence of the company had informed me from the observation post Smok that they came under attack by machine-gun and sniper fire. I immediately informed the commander of the battalion, who ordered me and my deputy to climb up to the position and perceive the situation." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And then later on in the document, you go on to describe further observations and actions that you took, and then towards the bottom of the document there's a paragraph that starts with, and this might be on the second page of the Macedonian, a paragraph that starts with: "At about 1100 hours ...," which I think is towards the middle, that's not being displayed right now: "At about 1100 hours, our positions came under fire of 82-millimetre mortars, and during this the grenades were falling at our positions. We realise that the fire was coming from the small forest near the village. After being ordered, the deputy fired five projectiles against the positions of the mortars of the terrorist groups, and after the fifth grenade the attack stopped." And then the last sentence of this report says, if we could perhaps move the document up so the witness could see it: "Further on, our activities against Ljuboten village had stopped. The police are undertaking the further activities." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is this report in accord with the actions taken by your company on 12/8/2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, this had previously been marked for identification purposes. Could we tender this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Following up on this report, Mr. Jurisic -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P306, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Following up on this particular report, Mr. Jurisic, did the battalion also keep a diary or log regarding the events that occurred within the battalion's area of command?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could please show Mr. Jurisic P00305. It is tab 13 of today's binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, do you see this first page? It says: "Military Diary of the 3rd Guardist Battalion." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if we could turn to page 4 of the English, I believe it's page 3 of the Macedonian, and the hard copies it's page 4 of the English. The left-hand portion. Yes, thank you. Mr. Jurisic, do you see -- you have hard copies as well, in case the resolution on the computer screen is not sufficient for you. Do you see, in the right-hand corner, there's an entry here, and along the top it says "Date", "Contents", "Source", "Remarks", do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you see an entry here that says "12/8" under the date column, it's the very first entry?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you see that in the "Source," it says: "Commander of the 2nd Company," do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And this person would be you, is that correct, the commander of the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you recognise this entry in this first page that I showed you as the diary of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should read it first.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. Jurisic, let me ask you a few questions first. Do you recognise the handwriting that's in this particular entry that I've directed your attention to?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could just read to you what it says, it says: "At the period of time between 1100 until 1700 hours during the ..." And there's a portion that's illegible: " ... of the members of the MVR" - which is Ministry of Interior - "in Ljuboten village, the terrorists were firing from ... " And it says something that's illegible. " ... and Jecmeniste towards our positions with 82-millimetre mortars." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "At the end of our company, 12 mortar shells had fallen. We fired back with 120-millimetre mortars and 76-millimetre cannon toward the positions of the terrorists." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Do you recall anything with respect to this particular report, and that is that the terrorists were firing from Jecmeniste?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if you can look at the handwriting, is there also a reference to the village of Kulm, K-u-l-m?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't notice any such thing. Yes, it is mentioned, I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the mention with respect to the village of Kulm and the village of Jecmeniste is that these are the positions that the terrorists were firing from, is that correct, from what you read?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we found it -- found out about it afterwards, after the actions were finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If I could show you -- that's already been admitted, so if I could show you another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you move on, could I ask: What mortars did you have in your company at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we only had 82-millimetre mortars, so mentioned here are also 120-millimetre mortars, which were not under my command, and I don't know why would I give or be a source of such mortars, because they were not under my command, those mortars of 120 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In which unit were the 120-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were in the same battalion where my company was, and it is a support battery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So in your company, you had lighter mortars, 82-millimetre; the heavy mortars were in the support mortar company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So are you saying that you did not order the firing of these 120-millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I haven't issued such order, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What of the 76-millimetre cannon? Were they in your company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had two such cannons in my company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you give orders for their firing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but only when we were under attack, and my commander was informed about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And what were the targets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The targets for cannons are usually the most risky position. In this case, it was an 82-millimetre mortar that was firing at us. That was the main target for the cannon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And where was this 82-millimetre mortar firing at you, where was it located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me explain, Your Honours. When they started firing at us, we did not know where were the shells impacting on us coming from. They started impacting, and we measured the sound and the time that the projectile was flying, we measured the distance, and it approximately fit. The sound and everything indicated that it was in the forest behind the graveyard. I then consulted with my other superior officers, and we believed it was there, but to this date I'm not sure whether the mortar was located there or not. So we fired several projectiles to the small forest or behind the small forest next to the graveyards. After that, much later, maybe it was the 10th or the 12th grenade or something, one of my soldiers who had a higher position, he noted some movements in the area where I supposed the mortar was stationed. After that, I just communicated this to my commander, where could the mortar have been, because it did not stop firing. Immediately afterwards, since 120-millimetre mortars are not under my command, I had no right to issue an order, so it was my commander who asked for assistance. He ordered the battery to support me because I was direct attack of other mortars. So the battery opened fire to this additional, added targets. These are Kulm, the hill where the mortar was firing from, we believed it was firing from there, and later we discovered there a quantity of ammunition, equipment, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, just to follow up, then, you said that there was fire towards Kulm. What about Jecmeniste which is referenced here in this report?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was like this, I think, as far as I'm able to remember at this moment: There are two locations in close proximity to one another. The exact position of one of the mortars you will not be able to pinpoint. It is behind some shelter or something, so you need to cover a larger area in order to neutralise the mortar. So I think it was in this context that the two positions were mentioned, because essentially nobody was really sure where the mortar was located. This is my personal opinion. It is not necessarily accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And I apologise to the court reporter. I should have spelled the location. It's J-e-c-m-e-n-i-s-t-e. That's the location I was referring to. Mr. Jurisic, did the 1st Guardist Brigade also keep a diary with respect to events that had occurred in the brigade's responsibility area?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose, yes. I have never seen it myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we just ask for five minutes' break until I bring the court files into the courtroom, because I will use them and the witness will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will stay here, but you can send for the court files, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much once again, Your Honours. I would like to ask for the assistance of the usher in distributing the court files to the Judges and to the witness, and we have some for our colleagues. But it might not be in the best order, and I hope that with the assistance of the list, the Prosecutor will be able to follow my questions. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Jurisic.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic, and I am counsel for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Mr. Jurisic, before I start asking you questions, I will ask you -- I would actually ask that both of us are mindful of the interpreting of what we are both saying; namely, I am sure that you're able to understand the language that I'm speaking, as I understand the language that you are speaking, but my questions and your answers as well need to be interpreted for The Honours and the other colleagues in the courtroom to be able to know what we are discussing. So I would kindly ask you to make a brief pause after I have asked my question and wait for the question to be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the answers to the questions of my learned colleague, I understood that you graduated from the military academy and you're a professional military officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When did you graduate from the military academy and where?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I graduated in 1999 in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you started -- when did you start serving in the Army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: August 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From your previous statements made in 2004 to the investigator of the OTP, and my learned colleague refreshed your memory about them, I think you stated that in 2001 you had your specialisation. Could you please tell me what specialisation it was, and where did you take that education?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just ask you, are we speaking about France, because in 2001 I had my specialisation in France.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any other additional vocational trainings or specialisations?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In 2001, I was in France to specialise in anti-armour rockets, and after that I was at many places in many countries. Should I enumerate them all?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So would it be correct if I stated that apart from the military education that you earned in your own country, in the Republic of Macedonia, you have additional military skills that you earned abroad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Turkey, Germany, France and Hungary.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is possibly a mistake in the transcript. I asked about NATO countries. In line 22, that fact was not noted in the transcript, but the witness replied to it and enumerated the countries. At the beginning of your testimony yesterday, my learned colleague the Prosecutor asked you whether, in 2001, you saw the orders issued by the President of the Republic. Do you remember that you were asked that question?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you answered that you, personally, have never seen such orders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Jurisic, you can agree with me if I stated that you do know that the President of the Republic of Macedonia is at the same time the commander-in-chief of the armed forces of the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also know that in this capacity, he was able to issue orders to the armed forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can also confirm that he was able to issue those orders from his capacity as commander-in-chief of the armed forces both verbally and in writing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it would also be correct that the President, in his capacity as the commander-in-chief, could issue order to any subordinate officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that apart from the Constitution that stipulates that the President of the Republic is the commander-in-chief of the armed forces, the rights, the duties and responsibilities of the President are regulated additionally with the law on defence and other secondary legislation items, and to the best of your recollection this is also correct; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the law on defence, of particular importance for the operations in the army are also the rules of service in the Army of the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jurisic, that in 2001, in the Republic of Macedonia, the law on defence, adopted in 1995, was in force and that towards the middle of that year a new law was adopted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 2, 65 ter 1D443 in the Macedonian version. The English is 1D4083. That is the English version, while the Macedonian is 1D4079. Your Honours, for the purposes of this cross-examination, we prepared a draft translation of two articles only, and I wish to show them to the witness. When the official transcript is ready, we will replace them. You see now the first page from the collection of regulations governing the defence, so I would like to ask to move immediately to the second page. In Macedonian, that is 1D408, and in English it is 1D4084. The English page is 1D4085. These are the initial provisions from the law on defence, and at the bottom you can see this is a law that, as you have stated, was published in the Official Gazette of Macedonia in 1995. Is that the law that you mentioned before, the law being in force in 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask to turn to the next page of the Macedonian version, 1D4081. And you see here the Article 15 that provides for the duties of the President of the Republic. Please look at the Item 12. I will read it out to you: "Among the other competences of the President is to order use of police to carry out military tasks in a state of war." Were you, as an officer, as a military officer, aware that the President of the State, as commander-in-chief, had under the law powers to order use of police forces?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you to also turn to the next page in the Macedonian text, that is, 1D4082, and please look at the Article 23: "The aforementioned article states that in a state of war, the police can be used to carry out military tasks as a component part of the army." And below this article there is a reference to the powers of the President as a commander-in-chief, and that is law. Were you, as a military officer, aware that in a situation when the police carries out military tasks, combat tasks, it is also under the command and control of the army structures?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I would seek to tender this portion of the Law on Defence into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 1D97, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you have just stated, towards the middle of the year a new Law on Defence was adopted, a new Law on Defence of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, before we look at the relevant provisions, is it correct that after the adoption of the law, there are numerous secondary legislation items adopted in accordance with the legal system of the Republic of Macedonia, and it is them who actually make possible for the law to be enforced in the practice?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when it comes to the Army of the Republic of Macedonia and other defence forces, then it is necessary to adopt the Rules of Service and other regulations that actually govern the modes of enforcement of the law and also the modes for the system of command and management; is that understanding of mine about the way in which the law operates correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab number 1, and that is 65 ter 788. R042 -- oh, we have it already, 4542, and the English text has also appeared on the screen. Do you, Mr. Jurisic, recognise the Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia, which is the publication where laws and other regulation of the Republic of Macedonia are published?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you see that this Official Gazette was actually published on the 1st of June, 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in it, the Law on Defence that we just discussed was published; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask now to look at the transitional and final clauses of this law that are in the Macedonian R424549 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 424559.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- while the English is N0022850. These are the provisions from Article 172 to 174. Mr. Jurisic, let's look at the Article 174 first, where it is noted that this law enters into force on the eighth day after the publication of the Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia. You do know that this is a general rule when laws come into force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But I would like to ask you to look together at the Article 172 and Article 173 of the law. The Article 172 provides regulations, the issuing of which is foreseen by this law will be issued in the period of one year from the day it enters into force, except for the regulations provided for in Articles 142, 143 and 144 that will be adopted within two years. And the Article 173 stipulates that at the date this law enters into force, the validity of the Law on Defence ceases and, in brackets, it is the law that we have mentioned before, that is, the law of 1995. And the paragraph 2 stipulates: "Regulations are passed on the basis of the law and paragraph 1 of this law will be applied until the regulations from Article 172 of this law are adopted, unless they are in contravention to the provisions of this law." Mr. Jurisic, is it correct that the prior version of this law was in force, in accordance with these provisions right now, all the way until the moment these secondary legislation items were adopted, those mentioned in this provision? Were you aware of this or do you know it from your practice from 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of this, and it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you now to look at the Article 18 of this law, which you can find in Macedonian page R0424544, and the English page is N0022789. As one can see from the text of the law in Article 11, it regulates the authorisations and the rights and the obligations of the commander-in-chief of the army, the President of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the transcript said "Article 11", and it should say "Article 18".

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at this article, Mr. Jurisic, so that we won't have to go into it as a whole, you can note that the authorisation of the President of the Republic to order the use of police force is no longer foreseen with this article. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask you to look at the last item of this article, where it is stated: "In order to realise the function in the area of the defence, the President of the Republic and the commander-in-chief of the Army adopts by laws our secondary legislation."

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, is it correct that until the president of the Republic adopted the regulations stated in this provision, he continued exercising powers in accordance with the previous law. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now about the Article 19, which is in the same Macedonian page, while the English page, apart from the page that we see here, continues also on N002-2790. And I kindly ask you to look now and read about the powers of the government of the Republic of Macedonia with regards to the police in Macedonia, and that is the Item 11, while in the translation it would be on the page N002-2790, line 8, where it says: "Orders to use the police forces." So in Item 11, it is stated that the government of the Republic of Macedonia orders the use of police in a state of war in support of the army?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct -- and my understanding is that the competences of the President, pursuant to the law, were transferred to the government of the Republic of Macedonia, but the actual application or use of these powers hinged on the adoption of the secondary legislation items; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jurisic, that neither the old nor the new Law on Defence provide that the Minister of the Interior had powers to order the use of police forces for military purposes or for combat tasks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I spent five minutes in bringing of this file, and should we now take the recess or should we continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We would be able to go five more minutes on the tape, but could I look ahead and ask: Is it the expectation of counsel that we will finish the present witness today?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, considering that my learned colleague finished earlier, my understanding is that I will be able to finish within the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Apostolski, do you anticipate being long with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that I will need one hour for this witness, so we will do our best to be in coordination with my colleague Residovic and finish with the witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I take it that will accommodate your needs probably, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I ask those questions with reason, in that as counsel may be aware, I sit in other matters as well, and a matter, I am told, has arisen of some urgency, which may require me to be dealing with something else on Monday. And perhaps, Ms. Motoike, if you could discuss with Mr. Saxon, who is at the moment, I understand from last night, looking at the question of the future timetable and estimates of the length of the Prosecution case, and while it's too early yet for me to know exactly what will be the demands on my time on Monday, it may well be the case that I am not able to sit in this matter, so the prospect arises whether it would create too much of a difficulty if we did not sit on Monday. And it would certainly help in that direction if the present witness were able to be finished by the end of today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before we go on with the questions, I would ask 45 ter 88, the new Law on Defence, be accepted as evidence of the Defence. Correction. The law is 65 ter 788. This is after the first tab in the binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 1D98, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, on the question of my learned colleague, you said that you were on duty as commander of the 2nd Company of the 1st Guardist Brigade the beginning of July 2001. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that prior to your assumption of duty, the command was -- the Defence Command of Skopje was established?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The defence of the city of Skopje was otherwise of strategic interest for the Republic of Macedonia; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The decision to undertake special measures for the defence of the city of Skopje and its environment was also of strategic significance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at the document which is after tab 8, 65 ter 646, number -- the number in the Macedonian version is 602677.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the number in Macedonia is N0026077.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see this is a decision brought by the President of the Republic on that date?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the right corner, lower corner, is the signature of the President of the Republic?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the title of this decision, it is established the basis for the passing of this decision and the aim of taking timely measures for the defence of the city of Skopje, which was due to the reason that -- which was the reason for the adoption of this strategic decision; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Point 2 of the decision, it lists the units that will care for the defence of the city, including the 1st Guard Brigade, which included your company, is this correct, that they be subordinated to it?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask that this be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 1D99, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at the document at tab 9. This 1D81. I would ask you to look at the first size 00694, Macedonian, and 1D3048 in the English version. Before we look at this document, I would ask you, is it correct that on the basis of this strategic decision, passed and adopted by the President of the Republic, subordinate levels brought operative decisions and determining the missions of these units, and which you, as military officers, obliged you for the carrying out of these duties?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask you to look at -- together at these documents. Do you agree with me that in the upper left corner is that this decision was adopted by the city of Skopje, the Defence Command, on the 11th of July, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that this is on the order for the defence of the City of Skopje? This is the text which is located in the middle of this document; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at the last page of this document, Macedonian 0006 -- this document number is N000-6918. My apologies. 1D053 -- 3053. Line 23 of the transcript is wrong. The document -- the 11th of June is the date of the document. Mr. Jurisic, in the lower right corner is a signature of the commander, Major-General Sokol Mitrovski. Is General Mitrovski, in accordance to your understanding in the first year, was he the commander of the defence of the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask that we go back to the first page of this document, N00-6913. The English, 1D3048.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, let's look at Item 1. It lists as follows: "As a consequence of the establishment of and actions by the armed formations of the Albanian minority on the territory of Kosovo, and the choice of armed violence as a method for resolving possible dissatisfactions and political demands on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia, for a long period of time diversion terrorist groups of the Albanian minority are active with mixed composition, both by motives as well as by origin. Their strength varies." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Further, it states: "Because of defeats incurred with the security forces with the Republic of Macedonia in the populated areas in the eastern slopes of Skopska Crna Gora, there are noticeable efforts on the parts of the terrorists to transfer the actions to the region of Skopje and to facilities of vital importance for the normal life of the population and the operation of the bodies of state authority. Terrorists control the village Aracinovo where it follows --", followed by the text as it is listed in the document. In accordance to your understanding from 2001, Mr. Jurisic, are these the basic reasons for which this command for the defence of the city of Skopje established?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is quite -- this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at Item 2.2. In paragraph 2, it lists, and I quote: "Task. In joint action, with the neighbours and bodies of the Ministry of Interior Affairs -- Internal Affairs -- and Civil Defence, to control the access points towards the city of Skopje, to destroy the discovered diversion and terrorist groups, and to hinder the infiltration of diversion and terrorist groups into the city and into the region of vital facilities and actions upon these." Is this the basic task which you also were charged with when you took over the company in the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at the other page of this document, 1D3044, and 49 in the English version. Let's look at this Point 3, fourth paragraph, where it is stated: "The forces of the Ministry of Interior will block the village of Aracinovo and will control the entrance into the village." Is this way of elaborating the attacks of the Ministry of Interior clearly speaks that the units of the Ministry of Interior were under the command of the army and that the army determined and issued military combat tasks to this unit for the defence of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, this order is order which clarifies or underlines what you responded so far regarding the manner of engaging the police force on their combat duties, combat activities?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The listed task given to the army of operative significance, and this is to control the access to the city, towards the city of Skopje, to destroy diversion and sabotage groups, and to impede infiltration of diversion and sabotage groups, is practically a task which is elaborated in the order of your brigade, and this was your basic task during the time when you came to the region, which you pointed out to our colleague yesterday, in the area of Ljubanci and Ljuboten; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For the superiors of -- officers of lower rank, commander of the defence of the city of Skopje, was it not necessary to issue additional orders so that this basic task can be carried out? This was their basic duty, to impede terrorists from entering Skopje and to destroy all and any terrorist groups that is present in that area, that they would discover in that area; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In answering to the question of my learned colleague, you also mentioned that when you assumed the position of commander of the 2nd Company of the 3rd Battalion of the 1st Guardist Brigade, your brigade was deployed in the area, listed area, do you recall that, when you made the statement?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at the document which is after tab 10. This is 65 ter 647, Macedonian version N0026078, the English ET. Mr. Jurisic, is it correct that under the authority of the President of the Republic, as the commander-in-chief, is also the mobilisation of the army?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document which you have in front of you, also in the upper left corner, issued by the President of Macedonia, and the right-hand corner contains -- in the lower corner is the President of the Republic of Macedonia; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the order issued on the 11th of June, 2001, mobilisation is ordered, among others. If we look at Point 1, of the 1st Guard Brigade, and this is the brigade that included your battalion; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Practically, this order was the implementation of decision of the President for the formation of the defence of the city of Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In regards with the mobilisation, Mr. Jurisic, is it correct that there was substantial problems in calling for the reserves of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were certain problems in terms of quantity and quality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When talking about the quality of reserves, will you concur with me that I say that because of the fact that a very small number of persons called on the -- responded to the call for mobilisation, the criteria were often lowered, and persons were mobilised which, under different conditions, would not have been mobilised but were so because of the needs of the country, the demands of the country?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the reserve forces in the units, the actual composition of them, were changed at every 30 days?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is, if I can say it in this way, and please answer whether you agree with me, this was a very big problem for the commanders, for the leaders, regarding the training and regarding the effective control over them?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in your company, you also faced this problem; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask you now for the 65 ter 647 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 1D100, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Jurisic, during your testimony, you recognised, in the sketch in the map that my learned colleague showed to you, the position of your company, the place where the command of the company was located, and the place where the company was stationed, in general, but also all the monitoring points that you had occupied at that time.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, observation posts instead of monitoring points.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Jurisic, that after the deployment of your company, and pursuant to the order on defence of the city of Skopje, you undertook significant tasks of reconnaissance and gathering data about the surroundings and especially about the sabotage and terrorist groups; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In preparation for this trial, on the 3rd of July, 2007, you stated to the Prosecutor that immediately after the arrival, you would receive from your soldiers, several times a week, information about the movements of the NLA in the area where your company and your battalion were deployed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The reports that you received from your soldiers spoke to the fact that they noticed movements of people wearing black uniforms in that area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, it was known that the NLA members were wearing black uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, armed people were noticed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the reports that your subordinate officers would make to you support the fact that movements towards the village of Ljuboten were observed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, you would receive reports that villagers are leaving the village with a large number of cattle, especially sheep, and then they returned to the village with significantly less sheep; is that correct also?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is not only the information I received, I personally have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, these so-called shepherds would come close to your positions and they would put the security of your company at risk; is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. If I make it more precise, Your Honours, if I'm allowed. Actually, those persons, those shepherds, were, in a way, in -- in my view, they were the eyes of the terrorists, because in that way they were counting the people at our positions, the deployment of our forces, et cetera. I end it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So what you had stated for me means that they were monitoring your combat positions and they were informing the NLA about it?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from these reports, is it also correct that the soldiers had found, in the area where the soldiers were moving, live ammunition of Chinese origin that, in your understanding, was probably falling down from the trucks, from the transport vehicles during the transport?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And can I also make further clarification here, Your Honours? It was not only my soldiers. I personally found ammunition of Chinese production that fell off the vehicles. In principle, in the army, Chinese ammunition is prohibited, so this was not our ammunition. It was ammunition which was found several times and I personally have found when making reconnaissance of the grounds, and my soldiers have as well. I end here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct for me to state that these reports, these findings and your personal insight into some of the aforementioned facts, actually created in you a deep conviction that Ljuboten is used as a logistic base for the needs of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the other hand, it is also correct that you made efforts to explain to the population, to the inhabitants, that they are under no risk from you, unless of course the terrorists are entering the village and using it for actions against the security forces?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even the minor incidents perpetrated by your soldiers, particularly the reservists, you tried to resolve those incidents in a peaceful way with the village leadership; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in your exchange with the Prosecutor a while ago, you mentioned that a cow was killed, and then on that occasion you personally went to the village to resolve the situation, and the soldier was removed from the unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. And if I may add, also measures were taken against him, not only that he was removed from the unit but he was also surrendered to the law enforcement so that further measures are taken against him.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the notes of the 3rd of July that my learned colleague showed to you this morning, there is also a conclusion or, rather, a statement of yours that you personally were in a situation of entering the village of Ljuboten and being blocked, in a way. Can you tell us what is it about, Mr. Jurisic?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is actually the following, Your Honours: In the stage of my research or investigation of the situation about the cow that was killed in that region by my soldiers, I went into the village, together with the village leadership, village authorities, and we went to the scene of that incident to see who shot, from where, and what were the circumstances under which this happened. And after taking all the data and all the evidence, me and my driver, of course unarmed, I went back to my command station. And then I was literally blocked in the village. These are narrow lanes. A tractor came in front of me. We immediately tried -- because it was suspicious, I expected something could happen, we tried to drive in reverse. But when we turned back, there was a second tractor there that was blocking my way back. There was a small lane leading to the right, towards the exit from the village, towards the valley, but I was also blocked there because there was already a person there with a carriage who was blocking the way. So there were several seconds, several moments -- it was not a long period, but to me they seemed long, and I realised that it was actually dangerous to be there. My initial idea is I'm now being reminded of it, I think at that time I thought that something would happen to me. Fortunately, nothing happened. After that, after they looked at me, all three of those drivers of those tractors and trailers, one by one they moved away from the road and they let me pass. That is my experience from the village. So even if I went out, even if I -- went out of the car and started running, I couldn't go anywhere because there were high walls, stone walls, thick walls, protecting the villages all around me, so I couldn't go anywhere, forward, backwards, to the side. I couldn't go anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification.
