From this experience of yours, this situation where you entered the village to peacefully resolve a situation, would it be correct for me to infer that already then, in July or the beginning of August, depending on when this event you described took place, would it be correct for me to say that in the village of Ljuboten there were already ways established to block entry into the village and that one could not enter the village freely or move around the village freely?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned that there were walls around you. As a military officer, could you tell us, these walls that are customarily found around the Albanian houses and villages, or at least are around most of the traditional houses of the Albanian families, can they be considered a fortification of sorts when considered in a defence sense or in an offensive sense, a fortification for the persons located behind these walls?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that you couldn't move anywhere because the lane was narrow. Could you tell me, please, whether the width of the lane, of the street, would provide for a normal manoeuvre with a normal car?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is a single car, by driving carefully, yes, you can manoeuvre without any problem. But if it is a larger vehicle or two vehicles, it's difficult or impossible. I think they could not pass one another by or turn there in those lanes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if the vehicle in question would be an APC or a Hermelin, could they manoeuvre in such lane?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even if they tried, they would get stuck. That is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if someone would state before this Court, Mr. Jurisic, that those obstacles -- those objects that you mentioned as fortification of these facilities, they are actually walls to the family houses, that they were no obstacle because it would be very simple with a Hermelin to tear the wall down or tear the door down, would such testimony be accurate, in your opinion, considering that -- considering your knowledge of the situation and your experience?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understood. You are asking me whether it is possible to hit a wall with a Hermelin. This is nonsense, this is stupidity. My apologies, but this is not done. First, the Hermelin is not able to tear the wall down, and if it would attempt to, then it would remain on the spot. The Hermelin could not move afterwards. So what you're saying is illogical.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When we spoke about the composition of your company and the reserve forces, would it be correct if I stated -- before that, let me ask you: How many soldiers were there in your company?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this moment I can't remember the exact figure, but around 120, it might have been. More than 100. 100 to 120. I can't be more accurate than this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct that around 80 per cent of your company were made up of the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that within your company there was a large number of reserve forces from the neighbouring village, Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When my learned colleague, the Prosecutor, asked you, you stated that you have spent part of the 11th of August at your command post in the Children's Rest House in Ljubanci. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I start from the statement you gave to the Prosecutor earlier and say that you have spent most of the day there with the engineers team and the police near the place where the NLA have planted the mine at the Ljubotenski Bacila, then these facts would be correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And interpreter's correction, military police and not police.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You needed to remove parts of the truck that transported your soldiers there. You then took photographs of the scene of the incident, and you then investigated the immediate vicinity of the location where the mine was planted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And already that day you found, on that location, a detonator and a Zolja; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could it be inferred from this that these sabotage/terrorist groups, apart from the Zoljas and mines and mortars that you spoke about earlier, also used Zoljas?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that two days later, searching in detail the ground, you found, as you stated a while ago, numerous other things that belonged to the terrorists, some were pants, uniforms, ammunition, a passport, ID card, and that you handed these over to the battalion command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and there is, I think, a written report on it, on everything that I found.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, on line 52, 16, it should be automatic rifles instead of Zoljas.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When answering a question by my learned colleague, you spontaneously -- rather emotionally you explained your sentiments, how you experienced what happened to your soldiers on the 10th of August, 2001. Is it correct that part of your company that was returning from the position stepped on a mine that was planted at the location Ljubotenski Bacila?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And immediately the mine explosion killed six members of the company, one died on the way to the hospital, and the eighth died in the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Two of the soldiers killed were reservists from the village of Ljubanci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were informed about it by your subordinate officer, a platoon commander, Zoran Kitanovski [phoen]; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You immediately informed the commander, Despodov, about this event, and you then asked for a --

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I make it more precise?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could first the counsel repeat the final part of the question, because we did not get it, and could the witness be stopped?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not only that I asked for a helicopter, but I asked for combat assistance because the action was ongoing. So not only a helicopter to help us lift the injured, but also combat assistance because we were not able to remove the injured because we had information that they were under strong fire, that they were moving against them to finish the killing of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, you just explained the question I was about to ask. So it was not only the mine that was planted, but also the members of these terrorist groups continued firing at the injured, the officers, the survivors; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in response to this attack, you opened fire at their positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, you did not issue a single order to fire at the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But there was fire against your positions from mortars and other weapons from the NLA positions?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your positions, especially Smok and Bomba, were directly above the village. Is it possible, Mr. Jurisic, that the grenades fired at you could have hit the village, actually impacted in the village?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that you, as a commander, as you explained, were in a state of shock and for a long time afterwards and even to this date you can't forget what you have seen and what you have lived through, would it be correct for me to say that your soldiers were also in a shock and it was that event that provoked a horrific unrest, a horrific agitation on the part of the population of Ljuboten and the neighbouring village -- Ljubanci and the neighbouring villages?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note. Could the counsel and witness be asked to use make between the question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jurisic, we have been warned to make pauses, and we will try to accommodate the interpreters and make their job easier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Somewhat earlier, we discussed that it was difficult to put these reserve forces under effective command. Mr. Jurisic, in view of the position and the state in which these soldiers were in after the explosion of the mine, and although you had not received information, you cannot exclude the possibility that some of these soldiers from your positions opened fire towards Ljuboten with infantry weapons? Is it correct to say that this possibility cannot be simply excluded under such circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Jurisic, that you immediately, on the same day, on the 10th of August, 2001, that you received a report that three armed persons entered the village from the direction of the explosion and that they entered the village in the area of the Zendeli home?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at that time have knowledge that similar observations of entry of these persons into the village were also obtained by the police, who were on the -- in the check-points around the village?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably they had such understandings and knowledge, because all of the information I had, I transferred to my commander, I informed my commander about them, so most probably they too would have had the same information because I did not keep this information. All information I had was passed on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the entry, was it your presumption, when you heard this and when the others heard, that these are the persons who took part in the placing of the mines?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After you heard that these armed persons entered the village, did you then at that time believe that these are persons who took part and participated in placing the mines and then took shelter in the village?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I'm allowed to clarify. The reporting was -- for my soldiers, the report I received from my soldier was that in breaking up the group who took part in the attack on my soldiers and the placing of the mines and the killing of my soldiers, one group of these persons, because it was broken up, one part withdrew towards the forest, and the other part of the group down the valley towards the village. This is why I believe you are talking about the group who went down the valley towards the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And following the orders which we were looking at earlier about the defence of the city, this fact would be -- would represent a legitimate basis that you and other security forces carry out a search of the village and apprehend these terrorists; can you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have a number of other questions which are of a different nature than the ones we discussed at the moment. I would ask that the witness be shown evidence of the Prosecution, P5. The Prosecution exhibit, it's a picture which can be seen -- which can be seen behind tab 35. Do you see this picture, Mr. Jurisic?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the lower corner of the picture, you see bullet shells. In the upper part of the picture, you see a part of the house, the door, and to the left a wall of the house, the wall of the house. Is this what you see on this picture?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you, Mr. Jurisic, with the help of the Court Usher, to mark with a circle the place where the bullet shells are to be seen and to mark them with "1".

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mark with the number "2" the door to the house which you see on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And please mark with "3" the wall of the house, which is also shown on the left part of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There will be an overlap. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You marked part of the wall through the door, but that's fine. Thank you. Your Honours, I would like first to tender this exhibit, and then I will ask the related questions that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 1D101, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask the Registry to show us the lower part of this photograph in a somewhat enlarged version so that we can see the bullet casings. Once again, this is Exhibit number 5, P5. If you can enlarge the lower part of the picture, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, with the help of your professional expertise, professional knowledge and expertise, can you and will you concur with me if I were to say that here we have casings which come from a weapon of 62 -- 7.62 times 32 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is ammunition used for automatic rifles, AK-47, also known as a Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would ask you to clarify for me, or I want to check and test a fact. Tell me, is it correct -- and prior to that, let me ask you: Surely, you have used Kalashnikovs and this type of ammunition in your professional practice?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you know how bullet casings react when fired from these kind of weapons?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it also correct that when firing from a Kalashnikov and weapons of this type, the casings which are fired are automatically charged from the weapon?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When fired, one by one they are discharged from the weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that upon firing, these casings are discharged in an arc towards the right and somewhat forward; is this the manner in which these casings are discharged?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will repeat the question. It was not -- the question is: Is it correct to say that the discharge of the casings is at least two or three metres from the place where the shooter is located?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now ask that we look at the picture as a whole, once again, the one we were looking at previously.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we were to look at this photograph and the casings which are at the bottom of this photograph, in view of your previous response, would it be correct if I were to say that the shooter, whose casings are left here in this place, must have been at least two to three metres to the right of these casings?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would be two to three metres, depending where he was aiming, at the direction he was aiming at. If we know the direction of where he was aiming, we would know where he would be located vis-a-vis the casings.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The casings, if you had said previously are discharged to the right -- my apologies, my mistake. He would be then two or three metres to the left. Correct, my apologies. He would have to be two to three metres to the left of the place where these casings are?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the condition that he was aiming straight.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is exactly the manner of the shooting that I want to ask you about.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If the shooter is two to three metres to the left to the place where these casings are located, is it correct that then, due to the natural obstacle of the wall which you have marked, would not be able to hit the person who is at the door or nearby the door of the house?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Now I would ask the witness be shown Exhibit 5337. This is after tab 33. It's a document under seal. It should not be shown to the public. This is Exhibit 5337 -- Exhibit P337.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, in view of the fact that you are in the area around Ljuboten, that you have spent some time there around the period of 2001, you also had knowledge that the population of the village of Ljuboten deals mainly with agriculture; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that quite frequently, as part of their houses, there are also agricultural equipment, fuel for this equipment, stalls with hay and similar things; was this to your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Many of these things which I talked about are easily inflammable substances; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, as a professional soldier, whether it is correct that such materials could become inflamed also by a bullet from a cannon-ball or by a grenade, a mortar grenade?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It could also inflame by a bomb?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view, as you had said, that these houses are connected by walls, is it true to say that a fire in one of these houses, in one of these stalls, in one of these warehouses of fuel, can be easily transferred to other houses without these houses ever being hit by anything? Of course, if there is -- if the fire had not been put out, of course.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The photograph which you see in front of you, do you recognise this picture?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did not enter in the village of Ljuboten after the events?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If these were new buildings, would this be the street which you had passed when you went to the village to talk about the killing of the cow?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment, I cannot recall whether this is exactly the street, but most of the streets are like this. I cannot remember whether it is exactly this street which I passed through.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you can remember that this would approximately be the walls that you were talking about which surround the houses in this area in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall that the houses were in a range -- in a line as they are shown on this photograph, and this is what you had said previously, that the fire could easily spread from one house to another?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that this street was a very narrow one, and only in the areas where -- of a crossroads, such as we can see at the beginning of the lower left side of this photograph, only in places such as these, where two streets intersected, could vehicles, larger vehicles, manoeuvre; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Jurisic, I wish to thank you. Your Honours, I have finished with my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me ask you first, would it be better to go into recess now and then finish the cross-examination in one chunk or should I start now and then interrupt my cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We need to allow time not only for you, but for Ms. Motoike. I'd --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We could use a little time now with Mr. Saxon, have the break, but then it would be necessary for both you and Ms. Motoike to finish in the remaining period. Will that be feasible?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, yes, there won't be any problem with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will do that, then. Mr. Saxon, I see you sitting patiently. I think it would be convenient now if the witness would commence his break now, and his evidence will continue after this break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to the question that Your Honours asked me last night about the remaining time needed for the Prosecution's case, there are more than 40 witnesses who still remain on the -- what is called the Prosecution's proposed second amended witness list, and I am including in that number witnesses who have begun their testimony but have not finished, which I believe there are two such witnesses pending at this time. Your Honours, last night the Prosecution began a process of reviewing the evidence, the expected evidence, of those 40-odd persons, with a view to selecting more witnesses which could be removed from the Prosecution's case, and the Prosecution can say that already it feels that there will be a number of witnesses which it will be able to remove. But having said that, Your Honours, for obvious reasons the Prosecution would like to do this process carefully and methodically, and the process of review will be continuing during the weekend. And I would ask the Chamber's permission to report back to it no later than Wednesday of next week with a new proposed amended witness list as well as a new calculation for time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are, of course, not sitting on Wednesday. You meant you would be reporting in writing?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. We certainly appreciate that this is a matter which must be considered carefully and with proper care, so we thank you for the efforts you are making and look forward to the outcome. A secondary matter arose, Mr. Saxon. It's arisen for me because of the demands of another case that I'm hearing, and the question is: As it is anticipated, the present witness will be finished today, rather than being part heard to be finish on Monday, whether it will be disruptive if we do not sit on Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber can inform the parties, then, that we will not sit on Monday. That's coupled with the Tuesday and Wednesday that are at the moment not sitting days because of the commitments of counsel. I'm sorry about the loss of Monday, but given that it is just one day on its own, I trust that will not be too much difficulty. But there are demands which arise on the time of Judges in other matters, and this is one, and it is of some urgency. So we will not be sitting after today until Thursday of next week. We adjourn now and resume at a quarter to 1:00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness Mario Jurisic.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: My name is Antonio Apostolski, and together with my colleague, Jasmina Zivkovic, we appear for Mr. Johan Tarculovksi. Today, I will ask you questions related to the events in Ljuboten in August 2001. I would also like to warn you, I speak Macedonian language and that is the language in which you will be answering your questions, so please wait for the interpretation to finish and only then answer my questions to facilitate the work for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You were a commander of the 2nd Company of the 3rd Guardist Battalion in the 1st Guardist Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your deputy was Darko Brasnarski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 3rd Guardist Battalion was composed of three infantry companies and one battery. Commander was Mitre Despodov and his deputy, Sasha Isovski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 1st Company was stationed at Brodec, and the company commander was Saltamarski, Zoran; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Saltamarski, Zoran; yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The 3rd Infantry Company was stationed at Rastak, and the commander was Ferdo Pavlov; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The commander of the battery was Nikolce Grozdanov [sic]; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The battalion command was stationed at the school in the village of Ljubanci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It was located at the school, and you frequently visited the command, for meetings with the commander, Mitre Despodov; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you frequently went to the village of Ljubanci and you know it well?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In the village of Ljubanci, there is a football stadium or football playing field. Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that it is at quite a distance from the school, where the command was stationed?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the Exhibit P296.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Towards the middle of this sketch, can you see a place marked with "S-C-H-O-O-L," "School" in English?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see that next to it, from the left-hand side of it, there is the football field, as it is written?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there is no football field there at that location, it is not where the football field in the village of Ljubanci is located?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a problem with the orientation on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At the bottom of the map is the road to Radisani, as you can see. At the right-hand side of the map, there is the road to Ljuboten. To the left is the road towards Pobozje. The football field would be located at the other side of the street, across the street from the school. Is this correct that this is not the location of the football field in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me just a minute to focus on it. In my personal conviction, the football field drawn here is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Could you explain to us where is the football field actually located? Where on this map would it actually be located, in your opinion, from the school?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be to the right from the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could I ask for the assistance of the usher to help the witness use the stylus and mark the location of the football field.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly here. I can't be more precise because this is a sketch, but it should be somewhere here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness has marked in red the location of the football field. Your Honours, could this photograph be received in evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 2D28, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated that on August 10, 2001, when returning from their shift, eight soldiers were killed and eight were wounded. The soldiers were members of your company. Is it correct that the ambush was organised by the terrorist group NLA?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 100 per cent, I'm sure it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the NLA has perpetrated similar terrorist acts whereby there were Macedonian soldiers killed?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several such acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that after such terrorist acts were carried out, the NLA members would withdraw to settlements inhabited by Albanian population in order to mingle with the civilian population and it was part of their tactics and strategy?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that also before the terrorist attack of August 10, 2001, there were provocations directed towards the army, there was constant firing from infantry weapons against the army members, those who were under your command?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you receive the information -- those informations from your subordinate officers?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When asked by my learned colleague Residovic, you answered that after the terrorist attack you found a large quantity of weapons, explosives, Zoljas and other military equipment in the vicinity of the village of Ljuboten and that there is a report on that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 1D8D6 exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 1D86.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see -- in the bottom left corner, could the Macedonian page be moved upwards a bit, please? Can you see, in the bottom left corner, that there is the name of the commander of the 3rd Guardist Brigade, Major Mitre Despodov, the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That is your commander. Can you read the list of the explosive means and equipment found on the date of 14th of August, 2001, in the area of Ljuboten village, Ljubotenski Bacila?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, but could you please zoom it in a bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does this report correspond with the items found by you, that you then transferred to your -- handed over to your commander, Mitre Despodov?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Now I will ask you questions related to Sunday, August 12th, 2001. Is it correct that the positions of your company were attacked from the direction of the village of Ljuboten on Sunday around 8.00 in the morning on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that your positions were attacked with mortar -- with machine-guns as well as snipers from the direction of the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were attacked from the positions close to the mosque in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there was fire against your positions from machine-gun from the new houses at the northeastern edge of the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you personally saw the positions of the terrorists in the village of Ljuboten, where the shooting against your positions came from?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you use a binocular when observing those posts?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you see reflections from the fire coming out of the rifles?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you see, through the binoculars, people using weapons?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the photograph ERN N005-7605.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this photograph taken from the same direction where your positions were located? Is this the position where your positions were located?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you show me on this photograph -- can you pinpoint the locations where the fire was coming from, from the village of Ljuboten, at the positions of your company?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you say generally in which part of the village it is so that this part of the village could be zoomed in so you can make your markings more precise?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the start, at least, enlarge the photo around the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the Court Officer to zoom in to the mosque. A bit more. Thank you. It is fine now. Could you move back to the left a bit now? Fine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark the location where the fire was coming from against your position from the village of Ljuboten, could you circle it?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I indicate several positions where the fire was coming from?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to mark all the positions where the fire was coming from and which you have seen.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will now mark the positions regarding which I'm 100 per cent certain that fire was coming from, fire against us. [Marks] These lines at the bottom that I'm drawing was where they would move. This is generally where the terrorists would move when they were running away.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please make a single line and then mark that line with the number "1"?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And could you make an arrow to indicate where they were moving towards?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please use number "2" to mark the circle that you drew?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And could you please explain to us what was there inside that circle?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a machine-gun, as far as I can remember at the moment. It was rather active against us, and certain groups of - as far as I'm able to remember now - of about five people in black uniforms were running from there, and they would then be deployed across the line that I drew here, logically, because from up where we were located, when we found out that they were shooting from here [indicates]. They would be an easy mark, so it is only logical that they would run away and deploy around that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark another location, another position, with the number "3"?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was like this: There was one position in the vicinity of the mosque. I can't remember which exact house, but I will mark the general region where it was located, either a sniper or a machine-gun. Somewhere here was it [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark it? Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I could point another position. It is a bit further away from us, but there was a very active fire coming from there [marks]. It was this window of this house. I remember this 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you mark it with the number "4"?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] So these are the several activities that I could remember at this moment, while from this line, from the line number 1, there was a very active fire coming, very active.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The item 4 marks two houses. Was there fire coming from the both houses?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think from the upper one, from the new houses next to the road, the upper one in the circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. Your Honours, could I seek to tender this photograph into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 2D29, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you received an order from your commander, Mitre Despodov, and you acted, with your weapons, against those positions?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you consider them to be legitimate targets, these positions?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that despite the actions with the machine-guns, some individuals from the army were also using their personal weapons to fire at these positions?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, not "despite" but "apart from."

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You told me that Brasnarski, Darko, was your deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]. Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 00769.3?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And another interpreter's correction. In 75.16, it should be "mortars" and not "machine-guns."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn to the second page of the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see, at the bottom, the signature of Lieutenant Darko Brasnarski? Is that your deputy?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now turn back to the first page of the Macedonian version? This is a report related to the combat activities on August 12, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In this report or notice - I can read it to you - Darko Brasnarski says: "On the day of August 12th, 2001, in performing the regular tasks concerning the organisation of work during the day, we were informed, around 8.00 a.m., that at the check-point Smok, machine-gun and sniper fire was opened from the village of Ljuboten. With the company commander, Lieutenant Jurisic Mario, we immediately went to the check-points. I went towards the check-point Bomba and the commander towards the check-point Smok. When I went to Bomba, I received the task to prepare for any action that was about to follow, whereby I started the preparations. During that time, shots could still be heard from the village of Ljuboten towards the position Smok, and vice versa. Around 9.00, the mortar battery started to fire against the targets in the village of Ljuboten in support to our position. "Around 9.30, later sniper fire was opened against the position at B1 and a helmet was hit and punctured which was located on top of the sandbags." Does this report correspond to the information you had regarding that date, August 12th, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this report into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 2D30, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 00769.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please look at the second paragraph. First, in the bottom right corner there is the language: "Commander of the MFB, Captain Grozdonovski, Nikolce." Is it correct that he was the commander of the mortar battery?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This a report on combat activities on August 12, 2001. Do you see paragraph 2 in the Macedonian version, which starts with: "After ..." "After I carried out the necessary preparations, four of my soldiers and me occupied the observation point at around 8.30. At that point, the combat was still going on. Observing the village, I established that from around the region of the church, terrorists were opening fire. From around the old house, around 100 metres below the mosque, there was probably sniper fire coming, and above the mosque in the new four houses, in two next to one another, there was a machine-gun firing at us. Then I informed the commander about the situation and he ordered me to use several shells from the 120-millimetre mortars to destroy the targets. And between 900 and 1000 hours we fired several mines around the church, we fired eight mines -- we fired five mines against the sniper and I fired three mines against the machine-gun. In total, I fired 16 120-millimetre shells against the combat activities in the area of the village of Ljuboten." Does this correspond to the information that you possessed about August 12th, 2001, in the village of Ljuboten, and your views on it?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this report into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 2D31, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours and witness, Mario Jurisic, I have no further questions for you, and this is where I end my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, earlier this morning you were shown a document, and my colleague quoted from it. It is now referred to as 1D97, for the record, and it was on page 29 of the transcript of today. My colleague read out the portion that said, basically, it was a piece of legislation: "Among other competencies of the President is to order use of the police to carry out military tasks in a state of war." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: My question to you is: In 2001, had an official state of war been declared?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: On page 47 of today's transcripts, you also indicated that you had visited the town of Ljuboten I believe it was sometime in 2001. Could you please tell us around when that visit occurred?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last one was in cooperation with the local population to discover the cause for the disruption of their life, for the killing of the calf, and to discover the possible reasons for it. This was sometime in the month of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And besides the walls around some of the homes that you've described already to us, when you went into the village, did you see any trenches or bunkers?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I could not see because it was not possible to see because of the walls.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And on page 57 of today's transcript, you were also asked a question by my colleague. And after being asked the question, you agreed that based on orders you had looked at previously about the defence of Skopje, and the information that you had received about the persons who went towards the village after the mine had exploded, you indicated that that would represent a legitimate basis for you and other security forces to carry out a search of the village and apprehend these terrorists. Was such a search carried out by your particular battalion, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: On page 59 of today's transcript, you also were shown a photograph with some expended casings. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you were asked some questions with respect to the location of these particular casings, and that photograph, for the record, I believe, is P5. My question is: You said that it would depend on -- the position of the casings would depend on where the shooter was aiming. I guess my question to you would be: What would happen if the person who was shooting had another person standing next to them to the right, is it possible that casings could bounce off that person and end up in a different location than one would normally expect?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: You said that -- well, I guess my question is simply this: If a person was shooting from that particular type of weapon that you've already described, the casings go to the right, you said, the expended casings. If someone was standing to the right of the shooter, is it possible that casings could bounce off the person standing to the right and end up in a different location than one would normally expect?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: On page 54 of today's transcript, you also made reference to the mine explosion and that your positions were being fired upon on 10 August after this explosion. Could I ask you, how far is the location of where this mine exploded in relation to Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you precisely the distance. I don't know. I don't know the distance. One would have to measure it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can you give an approximation of the distance at all?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could perhaps say between 500 metres and one kilometre, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could we please show the witness what's already been admitted as P293. For the record, it's page 6 of the court binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Jurisic, do you recognise the area that's depicted in this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And there appear to be, in the photograph -- there's a crossroads where there's a white -- it appears to be like a wall that's in the middle part of the photograph. Is that the area where the explosion of the mine occurred?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you stated that there was fire against your positions from mortars and weapons from NLA positions after the mine exploded. By "your positions," do you mean the area that's depicted in this photograph, that is, where your injured soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Did your Smok and Bomba positions also receive grenade fire at that particular time?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall because there was a lot of confusion going on and I could not say. Everything which happened in other positions, I do not know. I was concentrating on this segment here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: In relation to this photograph, would your Smok and Bomba positions be depicted, if it was on the photograph, be depicted towards the top of the photograph, in the area?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would not be at the top of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, in what direction those positions were in relation to the photograph? Would they be to the left or to the right or towards the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The upper part of the picture, in the middle, where the ridges come together in this direction [indicating], but much lower. Since this is a hill and there's a downwards slope towards Ljuboten, therefore the positions were up the ridge, along the ridge which you see on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: They are not depicted in the photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIO JURISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not depicted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Motoike. Well, that is a quicker ending than we had anticipated. You'll be pleased to know, Mr. Jurisic, that that completes the questions that will be asked of you in this matter. The Chamber would thank you for your attendance in The Hague and the evidence you have given, and you may of course now return to your home and ordinary activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber, unless there is any other matter, will now adjourn, and we'll resume on Thursday of next week. I believe it is at 9.00 on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: 1.34 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 12th day of July, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.
